module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception, unless: -> { authenticated_by.bot_key? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authenticated_by(:session)
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def set_authenticated_by(method)
      @authenticated_by = method.to_s.inquiry
    end

    def authenticated_by
      @authenticated_by ||= "".inquiry
    end

The flakiness came from `with_raised_exceptions`, which changed the wrong setting. The full suite is now green in every order I tried, with parallelism left on.

## Root cause

Rails reads `show_exceptions` once, when it builds `Rails.application.env_config`. That hash is memoized (`@app_env_config ||= ...`), and every request merges it into its env. The helper flipped `config.action_dispatch.show_exceptions`, which is read only at that first build, so it had no effect on requests.

Whichever request happened to be first in a worker process decided the setting for the rest of that process:

- If a 404 test ran first, `:rescuable` was pinned, so `book_absence_test` got "nothing was raised".
- If `book_absence_test` ran first, its `:none` value was pinned, so the 404 controller tests raised `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`.

Since parallel workers are forked processes with their own memo, the failures moved around on every run.

I reproduced both symptoms deterministically with a serial run of three files under fixed seeds. The memo mechanics were confirmed with a runner probe.

## Fix

In `test/test_helper.rb`, `with_raised_exceptions` now toggles `"action_dispatch.show_exceptions"` in the memoized `Rails.application.env_config` hash, which is the value requests actually use. It saves the previous value and restores it in an `ensure`, so it holds when the block raises and when blocks are nested. Nothing was deleted, skipped, or weakened.

I also added `test/integration/with_raised_exceptions_test.rb` with three tests covering the promise: errors raise inside the block and render again after it, the previous value is restored when the block raises, and nested blocks restore the outer value. The first test fails on the old helper and passes on the new one.
